scope: Kebu Liguey (K066) acceptance case 7: English, French, Wolof interface coverage for the entire Liguey surface built so far (cases 1, 2, 4): worker profile, employer listings/applicant review, applicant applications, public discovery and listing permalink. Follows the exact pattern established for Network's i18n slice (Oct 15, lib/network/network-i18n.ts) rather than inventing a new one.
architecturalNote: Most Liguey pages are server components (auth check + data fetch) delegating to a client sub-panel for interactivity — unlike Network, which is entirely client-rendered. Only app/liguey/page.tsx had user-facing text directly in a server component; extracted it into a new app/components/liguey/liguey-home-client.tsx (receiving fetched data as props) so useLocale() and the translation dictionary can actually run there, following the same client-component-owns-the-text principle Network already established.
dictionary: lib/liguey/liguey-i18n.ts — a typed key union + Record<Lang, Record<Key,string>> dictionary (ligueyT), plus four separate enum-label maps (employmentTypeLabel, locationTypeLabel, applicationStatusLabel, listingStatusLabel) so stored/canonical values (employment_type, location_type, status) are never translated themselves — only their displayed label is, matching Network's needLabel/stageLabel/sectorLabel precedent exactly. The Wolof strings are an explicit, stated best-effort machine/assistant translation, not reviewed by a fluent native speaker — the file says so in its own header, and the existing LanguageBar 'AI translations are approximate' banner (HIGH_QUALITY_LANGS, already excluding wo) surfaces this in the running UI without inventing a second review mechanism.
componentsWired: app/components/liguey/liguey-home-client.tsx (new), liguey-profile-panel.tsx, liguey-discover-client.tsx, liguey-public-listing-client.tsx, liguey-applications-panel.tsx, liguey-employer-panel.tsx — every user-facing string in all six replaced with ligueyT()/label-helper calls, and <LanguageBar variant="builder" /> mounted on each (mirroring Network mounting it on both /network and /network/join, not just one page).

verifiedScenarios.dictionaryTests: tests/liguey/liguey-i18n.test.ts (9 cases, real unit tests against the actual dictionary, not samples): confirms every English key has a non-empty French and Wolof translation (no silent gaps); confirms no language defines an orphaned key absent from English; confirms all four enum-label maps cover the exact same value set across en/fr/wo; confirms ligueyT resolves per-language and falls back to English for any unsupported locale; confirms each label helper translates known values and degrades sensibly (not a crash) for an unknown value; confirms the canonical employment-type strings used in API payloads/DB comparisons are never accidentally the translated label.

fullSuiteResult: typecheck 0 errors; lint 0 errors/349 warnings (unchanged); vitest 6,021 passed/244 skipped (+9/+0 vs. the case-2 checkpoint — the 9 new passes are the dictionary-completeness test file; same 3 pre-existing hosted-QA-only failures); build confirmed separately.
stillOpen: No real-browser language-switching verification was performed for Liguey in this slice — unlike Network's Oct 15 slice, which added 4 new Playwright cases (French end-to-end submission, language-switch-mid-draft, Wolof rendering with the correction banner, blocked-storage resilience) to an existing recovered harness. Building an equivalent from-scratch browser harness for six new Liguey pages was judged out of proportion to this already very large session; the dictionary-completeness and label-correctness tests above are a real, honest, but narrower verification layer. Fluent Wolof linguistic review remains explicitly OPEN, exactly as for Network's Wolof strings — a passing test here is not linguistic sign-off. Real browser verification of Liguey generally (not just i18n) remains part of K066's unaddressed acceptance case 8.
